subject: Climate & Environment
title: Air Pollution and Lung Disease
description: A micro-lesson that makes Air Pollution and Lung Disease usable.

hook.text: A person in New Delhi breathes the equivalent of smoking 10 cigarettes a day just from the air.

buildup.text: Fine particles lodge deep in lung tissue, causing inflammation that never fully heals.

discovery.text: Chronic exposure leads to COPD, asthma, and lung cancer even in people who never smoked.

twist.text: Children's lungs develop until age 18. Pollution during those years causes permanent damage.

climax.text: Air pollution is the world's largest environmental health risk — bigger than unsafe water.

punchline.text: Breathing shouldn't be a health risk. For billions, it is.

quiz.question: Why are children especially vulnerable to air pollution?

details.summary: Chronic exposure to air pollution causes and worsens lung diseases including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and lung cancer. Fine particles and ozone inflame airways, reduce lung function, and accelerate disease progression over years.
details.whyItMatters: Air pollution is the largest environmental contributor to respiratory disease. Understanding the mechanisms helps explain why clean-air policies save millions of lives.
takeaways: PM2.5 and ozone are the pollutants most harmful to lungs
Long-term exposure reduces lung function even in healthy adults
Children exposed to pollution develop smaller lungs that never fully recover

faq.question: How does air pollution cause lung cancer in non-smokers?
faq.answer: Fine particles carry carcinogenic compounds deep into lung tissue, triggering chronic inflammation and DNA damage. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increases lung cancer risk even in people who have never smoked.

faq.question: Can lung damage from pollution be reversed?
faq.answer: Some inflammation and reduced function improve when exposure decreases, but structural damage from years of exposure is largely permanent. Children's lungs are especially vulnerable because growth lost during development cannot be regained.
